article.headline: Washington's $21 Billion Equity Bet on Chips and Rare Earth
article.lede: A financial tracker maintained by Unusual Whales, the market-analytics firm, shows the U.S. federal government now holds roughly $21.5 billion in equity across at least sixteen strategic companies — up 167% from the original outlay. The positions were assembled not through a sovereign wealth fund or a congressional appropriation but through repurposed semiconductor grants, defense contracts, and development-finance warrants. The Council on Foreign Relations calls it the largest American push into strategic industries since the Second World War.
article.body:
The portfolio is not, despite appearances, a conventional investment vehicle. Since January 2025, three federal agencies — the Department of Commerce, the Department of Defense, and the U.S. **International Development Finance Corporation** (*DFC*) — have converted CHIPS Act grants, restructured Defense Production Act contracts, and issued *warrants* (options to buy additional shares at fixed prices) into direct equity stakes across at least sixteen companies. The legal footing rests on statutory stretch-runs: the CHIPS and Science Act authorizes broad "financial assistance" to chipmakers; the Defense Production Act's Title III lets the Pentagon bypass normal purchasing restrictions "without regard to the limitations of existing law"; and the DFC's reauthorized charter explicitly permits minority equity stakes. Because all target companies agreed to the deals voluntarily, near-term legal challenges are structurally unlikely — Intel (INTC), having just agreed to cede 9.9% of itself to Washington, seems unlikely to sue its new patron.

The dominant position is Intel (INTC). In August 2025, the Commerce Department converted $5.7 billion in undelivered CHIPS Act grants and $3.2 billion from the *Secure Enclave* program — a classified Defense Department fund for dedicated domestic chip fabrication — into 433.3 million shares at $20.47 apiece. The government holds no board seat and votes in line with Intel's board on routine matters. Intel's subsequent recovery under chief executive Lip-Bu Tan, powered by AI data-center demand and a revived foundry strategy, has pushed the share price into territory implying an unrealized gain of at least $25 billion on that position alone, making it arguably the most profitable single trade in American industrial policy history.

The rest of the portfolio bets heavily on *rare earth elements* and critical minerals — the inputs China has been throttling through tightening export controls. The Pentagon paid $400 million for roughly 15% of MP Materials (MP), the only fully integrated U.S. rare earth operation, at Mountain Pass, California, and simultaneously committed to buying 100% of its neodymium-praseodymium (*NdPr*) output for at least a decade at a floor price of $110 per kilogram, roughly double recent market rates. A $35.6 million investment secured a 10% stake in Trilogy Metals (TMQ), which holds copper, cobalt, and zinc deposits in Alaska's Ambler Mining District. A separate $1.58 billion package — direct equity plus a loan — gave the government an 8–16% position in USA Rare Earth, a private Oklahoma company building a magnet factory in Stillwater and a heavy-minerals mine in West Texas. Trump's gloss on all this — "It's actually not that rare. There's a lot of rare earth. There's a lot of earth" — is geologically eccentric but the strategic anxiety is real: China controls roughly 60% of global rare earth mining and an even larger share of downstream refining.

Important caveats surround the eye-catching return figures. Every gain is unrealized paper profit; the government is in practice a locked-in holder — selling its 9.9% Intel (INTC) stake would be a market-moving political event. The tracker captures only publicly traded positions, leaving private-company stakes off the mark-to-market ledger, which means the full portfolio's true value is unknowable. Critics span the ideological spectrum: the libertarian Cato Institute warns that "the case for national security is not a case for normalizing a model in which politically favored firms receive public capital," while Democratic senators have demanded disclosure of whether administration officials hold personal stakes in the same companies. What nobody disputes is the precedent: for the first time since wartime industrial mobilization, Washington is a meaningful shareholder in the private economy — and the paper returns, however spectacular, cannot be cashed until someone decides to sell.

concepts.definition: A group of seventeen metallic elements — including neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and lanthanum — critical for electric motors, wind turbines, missile guidance, and consumer electronics. Despite the name, most are not geologically scarce; the problem is economic concentration: China controls roughly 60% of global mining and an even larger share of the refining and processing capacity that turns raw ore into usable materials.

A U.S. government agency established in 2019 to provide loans, equity investments, and guarantees supporting private-sector projects abroad — and, increasingly, domestically. Unlike its predecessor (OPIC), the DFC's charter explicitly authorizes it to take minority equity stakes in companies, making it the legal workhorse for some of the administration's minerals investments.

A 2022 U.S. law that appropriated $52.7 billion to revive domestic semiconductor manufacturing through grants, loans, and tax credits. The Trump administration controversially converted some undelivered CHIPS Act grants into equity stakes in Intel, an interpretation of the statute's broad 'financial assistance' language that the law does not explicitly contemplate.

A 1950 U.S. law giving the President broad authority to direct industrial resources for national defense. Title III explicitly allows the Department of Defense to make purchases and commitments 'without regard to the limitations of existing law,' a provision the administration has used to justify equity investments in minerals companies such as MP Materials and Trilogy Metals.

The two most commercially important rare earth elements, combined to make the high-strength permanent magnets found in electric-vehicle motors and wind turbines. NdPr oxide is traded by the kilogram; the government's guaranteed floor price of $110/kg for MP Materials' output represents roughly double recent market rates, effectively subsidizing domestic production against cheaper Chinese supply.

A contract giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to purchase shares in a company at a specified price before a specified expiration date. The government frequently received warrants alongside direct equity purchases, granting options to increase its stakes if certain conditions — such as a company changing control — are triggered.

A classified Department of Defense program that funds dedicated, physically isolated semiconductor fabrication capacity within U.S. borders for defense applications. The $3.2 billion contributed to the Intel deal from this program blended defense and commercial objectives in a single transaction, a structural novelty that critics say obscures accountability.

The increase in value of an asset that has not yet been sold. An unrealized gain exists only on paper and can evaporate if prices fall before the position is liquidated. In the government's case the problem is compounded: selling a 9.9% stake in a major public company would itself move the market and carry significant political costs.

article.fact_check: The three figures displayed on the Unusual Whales / Autopilot tracker — total value ($21.48 billion), dollar gain ($11.62 billion), and percentage gain (167.18%) — are internally inconsistent. If the gain is $11.62 billion at a 167.18% return, the implied cost basis is $6.95 billion, making the current value $18.57 billion, not $21.48 billion. Conversely, if 167.18% is applied to the $21.48 billion current value, the implied cost basis is $8.04 billion and the dollar gain should be $13.44 billion. The discrepancy most likely reflects a time-weighted return methodology that adjusts for the staggered timing of capital deployments across sixteen separate deals, rather than a simple cost-basis calculation. The tracker's methodology is not publicly documented. The broader direction of the claim — that government equity stakes have generated very large paper gains, concentrated in Intel — is well-supported by independent reporting from Bloomberg, Benzinga, and The Next Web. The poster's framing that the portfolio is 'all rare earth stocks and Intel' is also a slight oversimplification: the portfolio includes Korea Zinc, Lithium Americas, Westinghouse, and a partial stake in L3Harris's missile unit, among others.

ticker_intc.name: Intel Corporation
ticker_intc.blurb: Intel is the world's largest semiconductor company by revenue (historically) and the only major chip company that both designs and manufactures its own processors at scale. Its product portfolio spans PC and server CPUs (Core, Xeon), AI accelerators (Gaudi), FPGAs (Altera), and networking silicon. Intel's foundry ambition — Intel Foundry Services (IFS), renamed Intel Foundry — aims to manufacture chips for external customers on its 18A and 14A process nodes, positioning the company as a Western alternative to TSMC. After CEO Pat Gelsinger was replaced in late 2024, the company has undergone significant restructuring.
ticker_intc.recent: Intel reported Q1 2026 revenue of $13.6 billion, up from a depressed base, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.29 versus a near-zero consensus — the beat sent shares up 20%+ in after-hours trading. Data-centre revenue grew 22% YoY. Full-year 2026 EPS estimates of $0.48–$0.56 would represent ~101% growth from the 2025 base — a base-effect figure that reflects restructuring charges and near-zero profitability rather than a dramatic business inflection. Intel trades at ~62.1x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.61 given the distorted growth denominator.

ticker_mp.name: MP Materials Corp.
ticker_mp.blurb: MP Materials operates Mountain Pass in California, the only producing rare-earth mining and processing facility in the United States. The company extracts and refines neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) oxide and in 2025 opened a full-scale permanent magnet manufacturing plant in Fort Worth, Texas. Its customers include General Motors under a long-term supply agreement for electric-vehicle traction motor magnets, and the U.S. government has backed the company with roughly $400 million in strategic investment.
ticker_mp.recent: In early 2025 MP Materials inaugurated its Fort Worth magnet facility and began commercial NdFeB magnet shipments to GM, a landmark for domestic rare-earth supply-chain independence. The company's AI revenue exposure remains indirect — data-center cooling fans and robotics actuators use its magnets — but the robotics angle is drawing increasing investor attention as humanoid robot programs scale.

sources.title: 2025 to be a Defining Year for the Rare Earth Magnet Market — IDTechEx

ticker_tmq.name: Trilogy Metals Inc.
ticker_tmq.blurb: Trilogy Metals is a Canadian-headquartered base-metals explorer developing the Upper Kobuk Mineral Projects (UKMP) in the remote Brooks Range of northwestern Alaska. Its flagship assets — the Arctic copper-zinc-lead-gold-silver deposit and the Bornite copper-cobalt deposit — sit within the Ambler Mining District, one of the world's largest undeveloped polymetallic regions. The company holds a 50% interest in Ambler Metals LLC (joint-ventured with South32), which controls 100% of UKMP. In September 2025 the U.S. Department of Defense acquired a 10% equity stake for approximately $35.6 million, citing the copper and cobalt content as strategic to defense supply chains.
ticker_tmq.recent: The DoD investment in October 2025 sent TMQ shares from roughly $2.17 to a 52-week high of $15.21 CAD. The stock has since pulled back sharply amid permitting uncertainty — the Ambler Access Road, a 211-mile industrial road required for any commercial mine, remains contentious and faces ongoing legal and regulatory challenges from Alaska Native communities. Despite the government's endorsement, no construction timeline has been set, and the company is pre-revenue.
